economy.summary: As House Budget Committee Ranking Member, Boyle issues monthly statements criticizing the administration's tariff policies for keeping consumer prices high, saying families' cost of living has not come down as promised. He voted for the Inflation Reduction Act, which he described as lowering health care and energy costs for families.
economy.short: Criticizes tariffs for raising prices; voted to lower costs.

taxes.summary: Boyle opposed the Republican FY2025 budget resolution, calling it a $7 trillion tax giveaway to billionaire donors paid for in part by cuts to Medicaid and food assistance. He has also pushed for a wealth tax on the richest Americans and proposed reforming the debt ceiling process.
taxes.short: Opposes tax cuts for billionaires; supports wealth tax, debt-ceiling reform.

abortion.summary: Boyle supports abortion rights and called the Supreme Court's decision overturning Roe v. Wade a severe blow to women's rights and to individuals' ability to make their own health decisions. He is a cosponsor of the Women's Health Protection Act of 2025, which would protect abortion access nationwide.
abortion.short: Supports abortion rights; cosponsors Women's Health Protection Act.

education.summary: Boyle calls for increased federal investment in Philadelphia public school facilities, saying only Washington has the resources to fix aging buildings with asbestos, poor ventilation, and inadequate air conditioning, and he opposes cuts to federal public education funding. He founded the Congressional First-Generation Student Caucus and has secured federal funds for local universities.
education.short: Supports more federal school facilities funding; opposes education cuts.

healthcare.summary: Boyle voted against the 2025 Republican reconciliation bill, saying it enacted the largest cuts to health care in American history across Medicare, Medicaid, and the Affordable Care Act, with millions projected to lose coverage. He has announced legislation with a state lawmaker aimed at blunting the effect of federal Medicaid cuts on Pennsylvanians.
healthcare.short: Opposes Medicaid and ACA cuts; proposes legislation protecting coverage.

energy.summary: Boyle voted for the Inflation Reduction Act, calling it the largest clean energy investment in the nation's history and a driver of the transition to a clean energy economy. He opposes Republican efforts to repeal its clean energy and manufacturing provisions.
energy.short: Voted for clean energy investment; opposes repealing it.

guns.summary: Boyle voted for the Assault Weapons Ban of 2022, saying a ban on assault weapons and high-capacity magazines would save lives, and cosponsored the Bipartisan Background Checks Act and Enhanced Background Checks Act. He also voted for the Bipartisan Safer Communities Act, which he called historic and commonsense gun violence prevention legislation.
guns.short: Voted for assault weapons ban; cosponsors expanded background checks.

economy.summary: Arriaga proposes reducing the tax burden on working families, cutting federal regulations she says hurt small businesses, and expanding job training programs tied directly to local employers. She supports targeted infrastructure and industry investment to bring jobs back into the community.
economy.short: Proposes lower taxes, fewer regulations, job training, infrastructure investment.

taxes.summary: Arriaga supports policies that reduce tax burdens on working families. She also proposes greater transparency in how federal resources are allocated to cities like Philadelphia.
taxes.short: Supports reducing working-family taxes; proposes federal spending transparency.

education.summary: Arriaga says she will fight for federal support for career and technical education, workforce training, and school safety. She backs expanding partnerships between schools, unions, and local employers to create pipelines from classroom to career.
education.short: Supports career-technical education, school safety, school-employer partnerships.

healthcare.summary: Drawing on her career as an operating room technician, Arriaga aims to expand access to affordable care, reduce costs, and increase transparency. She supports strengthening preventative care and cutting bureaucratic barriers that delay treatment.
healthcare.short: Supports affordable care access, preventative care, cutting treatment barriers.

guns.summary: Arriaga says she will push for federal resources to help local law enforcement target repeat violent offenders and to expand community-based prevention programs. She supports funding mental health and addiction services alongside policing.
guns.short: Supports policing resources, prevention programs, mental health funding.
